equity_bridge.item: Unfunded pension and OPEB, after tax
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K funded status: US pension -$441m, international pension -$179m, other retiree benefits -$663m = -$1,283m pre-tax; ~22% tax shield -> ~-$1,000m. Debt-like; service cost already in EBITDA.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is meaningless for CL: total equity is ~$0.4-0.6bn against ~$29bn of treasury stock, because decades of buybacks and dividends exceed retained earnings. It diverges >30% from revenue and EPS by construction, so revenue CAGR (4.3%, mostly pricing in an inflationary window) is used instead. GAAP EPS 5yr CAGR is negative only because FY2025 carries the $794m after-tax skin-health impairment; base-business EPS grew from $3.60 (FY2024) to $3.69 (FY2025).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (no separate equity-award tax line; net debt so no interest strip). Owner FCF FY2020 $3,202m, FY2022 $1,735m, FY2025 $3,479m. The 3yr CAGR (26%) is off a FY2022 trough when working capital absorbed cash during the inflation spike; the 5yr CAGR (1.7%) is the honest underlying rate. SBC grew from $107m to $155m (2020-2025), faster than FCF, but at <0.8% of revenue it barely moves the owner-FCF series (adjusted 5yr CAGR 1.67% vs reported 1.90%).

scenario_narratives.base: Colgate grows at its long-run ~3-3.5% (pricing plus modest volume), with Latin America and Hill's carrying a flat-to-negative North America. FY2026 lands inside the 4-5% sales guide. Productivity-program cash charges trim margin through 2028; the savings are partly kept, returning pre-SBC EBITDA margin to ~25.5%, in line with the decade-long 21-22% base operating-margin band.
scenario_narratives.bull: The toothpaste franchise (~41% global share) holds pricing, Hill's therapeutic/premium pet food and Prime100 compound faster than the group, emerging markets (~45% of sales) keep volume growth positive, and North America stabilises. Program savings drop through, lifting margin ~1.8pp over the decade with growth ~4-4.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Staples become a share-loss story: private label keeps taking North America, skin health stays impaired, FX and hyperinflation halve reported growth, commodity and tariff costs outrun pricing, and talc litigation (561 pending cases, rising) produces cash outflows. Growth ~2%, margin drifts to 23.5%, terminal multiple 16x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A wide-moat, low-growth staple: value is dominated by the terminal multiple, so the house discipline is a 20x cap on base/bull terminal FCF (Gordon at 7%/2.5% would be ~23x) and 16x in the bear. SBC is small (<1% of revenue), so the house/street band is narrow. The equity bridge deducts net debt and the after-tax pension/OPEB deficit; NCI is charged in the flows. At a 15% hurdle the entry price for a ~3% grower lands well below intrinsic value by construction.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal multiple: each 1x on the base cap is worth roughly $3/share
North America private-label trade-down spreading to other developed markets
FX translation and hyperinflation (2/3 of sales non-US)
Talc litigation tail not reserved or modelled
Restructuring program costs already raised once ($200-300m -> $350-550m)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 75.96-101.18
data_sources.financials: SEC 10-K FY2023-FY2025 and 10-Q Q1 2024-Q3 2026 (research/CL/Extracted), CL_Metrics.csv from core_metrics
data_sources.qualitative: CL_Analysis.json (2026-11-08); Q3 2026 earnings guidance as summarised there

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares for Q3 2026 (799.7m, 10-Q Q3-2026 EPS note, line 1711). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Colgate is a steady repurchaser (FY2025 $1,210m; 9M 2026 $927m), so the flat count is actually funded.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement / equity statement 'Stock-based compensation expense' $155m (CL_Annual_FY2025.txt:3239); 9M 2026 $141m (CL_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:1372). Colgate publishes no separate line for taxes withheld on net-share settlement and no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC figure, so the add-back alone is used; the understatement is small at <1% of revenue.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.5 for a global household-products staple -> cost of equity ~6.8-7.0%; debt ~$7.7bn at ~3.5% pre-tax (~2.7% after tax) is ~9% of EV, pulling WACC to ~6.6%. Rounded UP to 7.0% and held identical across scenarios: FX/hyperinflation, talc and private-label risks are carried in the bear flows, not in the rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Under US GAAP operating-lease cost sits inside cost of sales/SG&A, so EBITDA is already after the lease charge; the $566m of operating lease liabilities (FY2025 10-K, line 4845) is therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. lease_cost_pct_path left at zero because the charge is already in the margin. Finance leases are immaterial and sit inside reported debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Net income attributable to NCI (Colgate-Palmolive India ~49% public float plus smaller subsidiaries) was $129m FY2025 and $91m 9M 2026, ~3.0% of base-business EBIT. Folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a +3pp leakage (23% cash tax + 3pp NCI = 26%); no NCI deduction in the bridge. Tie: FY2025 base EBIT $4,347m x (1-0.26) = $3,217m NOPAT vs attributable base-business net income $2,996m + ~$170m after-tax net interest = ~$3,166m, within 2%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company'; first valuation of CL, no prior DCF or memory entry). Global consumer staple with ~2/3 of sales outside the US; reporting and quote currency are both USD, so the adaptations file applies only for leases (B), NCI (flows) and the pension bridge. ANCHORS: FY0 = FY2025 (revenue $20,382m; base-business operating profit $4,347m = 21.3% margin, CL_Annual_FY2025.txt:2505; D&A $630m; SBC $155m -> pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA 25.2%). GAAP FY2025 EBITDA in the CSV ($3,936m) is depressed by the $919m skin-health impairment and $65m ERISA charge; the base-business figure is the right margin anchor. Balance sheet 30 Sep 2026: total debt $7,716m (MD&A line 2811: $532m current + $7,184m long-term), cash $1,527m, marketable securities $85m (added in the equity bridge). Owner FCF FY2025 = OCF $4,198m - capex $564m - SBC $155m = $3,479m; TTM to Q3 2026 reported FCF is ~$3,789m. Interest income ($75m FY2025) sits below operating profit and the company is net debt, so no interest-income strip is needed (it is outside the flows already). GUIDANCE (Q3-26, 30 Oct 2026): FY2026 net sales +4-5% (incl. low-single-digit FX tailwind, organic ~3%), base EPS +5-7%, capex ~3.0% of sales. Strategic Growth and Productivity Program: $350-550m pre-tax charges to end-2028, 80-90% cash, $200-300m annual savings -> modelled as ~0.5pp of margin drag in 2026-2028 (cash charges are excluded from base-business EBITDA, so they are put back into the path here) and partial savings retention thereafter. Working capital: Colgate runs negative operating working capital (-6.3% of sales at Q3 2026), so growth is roughly cash-neutral to slightly positive; wc_capture set to 0 (conservative, not crediting the float). Not modelled explicitly: talc litigation (561 cases, unreserved tail), the ~$165m IRS imputed-income dispute and Brazilian Kolynos tax disputes - carried qualitatively in the bear case and weights.

bear.narrative: North America private-label trade-down persists (organic -1.6% already), skin health keeps shrinking, and FX/hyperinflation (Argentina, Nigeria, Turkiye) strips reported growth to ~2%. Resin, oil and tariff-driven cost inflation outruns pricing and productivity, eroding the margin ~1.7pp to 23.5%; talc verdicts and the expanding restructuring bill absorb cash. Terminal multiple 16x for a structurally slower staple.

base.narrative: FY2026 at the 4-5% guide midpoint, then ~3.5% (2% price/mix + 1.5% volume, LatAm and Hill's offsetting a flat North America) fading to 3%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin dips ~0.5pp below the FY2025 base-business 25.2% while productivity-program cash charges run (2026-2028), then recovers to 25.5% as part of the $200-300m savings is kept and the rest is reinvested in advertising, as Colgate has historically done.
base.growth_rationale: Anchored to FY2026 guidance and the 10-year revenue CAGR of ~3%; the 2021-2025 4.3% was inflated by pricing.
base.margin_rationale: Colgate's base-business operating margin has sat in a 21-22% band for a decade; gross-margin gains are reinvested. No structural expansion assumed beyond partial program savings.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: 23% cash tax (FY2025 base-business ETR 23.1%; cash taxes paid $913m) + 3pp NCI leakage.

bull.narrative: Hill's premiumisation and the vet-channel moat compound at high single digits, Prime100 scales fresh pet food, LatAm/EMEA emerging-market volume holds, and North America returns to positive organic growth as innovation wins back private-label switchers. Most of the $200-300m program savings is retained and Hill's mix lifts the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 27%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): North America volume is already negative, cost inflation is renewed by the Middle East conflict, and the talc caseload is an unquantified tail. Base 50%: guidance was just raised and the franchise is durable. Bull 30% (below 35%): it needs Hill's, emerging markets and a North America recovery to all go right at once.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
